analysis.title: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (SPCX) Q3'26 Review: Strong Operating Momentum Across All Segments; SI Compute & Monetization Drive Another Quarter of Positive Estimate Revisions
key_insights: Reiterates Buy on SPCX and raises 12-month price target to $245 from $230 (65.8% upside from $147.79) after updated operating estimates. Shares are about 25% below the post-IPO peak closing price.

Q3'26 revenue ($14.575bn) and GAAP EBIT ($2.791bn) beat consensus ($12.809bn and $2.356bn), driven by AI segment cloud service revenue and Starlink adoption in Consumer and Enterprise & Government. Both came in below GS estimates.

Super Intelligence (SI) generated $7.56bn of Q3 revenue on 1.7GW of quarter-end compute. Management guides to about 2.5-3GW by YE26 and another 10GW+ in 2027, with an upside case of more than 20GW by YE27.
Management said new compute at current pricing pays back in under 1 year. Earnings call comments imply payback could fall to about 6 months in 2027 on lower build costs and higher monetization.

Demand for compute appears well ahead of supply. Short-duration contracts are renewing at higher $/watt, and management sees opportunity to rent its compute several times over. Internal vs external usage is expected near 50/50, with GrokBot potentially the largest internal consumer.

Power, cooling and electrical infrastructure are the primary bottlenecks, replacing chips as the constraint. Management targets infrastructure for 20GW of incremental capacity during 2027. Q4'26 capex is expected at $35-40bn, above GS and Street estimates.
Q1'27 revenue guidance of $33-37bn came in well ahead of GS and Street estimates and implies solid sequential growth toward management's $100bn December ARR target.
GAAP SI EBIT of $431mm missed GS ($2.736bn) and consensus ($777mm), largely due to elevated stock-based compensation tied to the Cursor acquisition.

Connectivity: Starlink Broadband momentum continues, with Starlink Mobile as the long-term opportunity on spectrum purchases and added satellite capacity over 2-3 years. v3 satellites plus Starship ramp are expected to deliver far more downlink capacity per launch, with management framing 100x current constellation bandwidth over three years. An investor teach-in on mobility could be forthcoming.
Space: Starship is the core economic enabler. Management targets weekly launches in 1H27 and roughly twice-weekly by end of 2027, with a Flight 15 goal of capturing both booster and ship.
SPCX and TSLA have each formed special committees of independent directors to discuss a potential business combination. GS offers no opinion on its likelihood or merits.

Estimate changes: FY27 revenue raised to $192.49bn from $127.46bn, GAAP EBIT to $79.16bn from $53.13bn, GAAP EPS to $5.52 from $3.96. Q4'26 GAAP EBIT cut to $4.71bn from $10.27bn and EPS to $0.44 from $1.02.

Valuation is a sum-of-the-parts on 2029 segment estimates discounted 1.25 years at 12%: Space 9.5x EV/Sales, Connectivity 20.0x EV/EBIT (from 24.0x), SI 25.0x EV/EBIT (from 28.0x). The SI multiple rises on a growth-adjusted basis to 0.65x from 0.53x on better compute-scaling visibility.

Funding needs from high capital intensity in 2H26 and 2027 are likely to act as an overhang on the stock until visibility on future capital raises improves. Stock drivers also include Starship launch data, broadband user growth, compute monetization and lock-up expirations.

market_movers.rationale: Reiterates Buy and raises 12-month target from $230 to $245 on updated operating estimates, citing a positive risk/reward skew with shares about 25% below peak post-IPO close.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported (21 Oct 2026 report): total revenue $14.575bn vs GS est $15.190bn and consensus $12.809bn (-4% vs GS, +14% vs consensus).
Q3'26 reported segment revenue: Space $1.767bn (consensus $1.458bn), Connectivity $5.248bn (consensus $4.917bn), Super Intelligence $7.560bn (GS $8.262bn, consensus $6.435bn).
Q3'26 reported GAAP EBIT $2.791bn vs GS est $4.667bn and consensus $2.356bn. SI GAAP EBIT $431mm vs GS est $2.736bn and consensus $777mm.
Q3'26 reported adjusted EBITDA $8.809bn vs GS est $9.163bn and consensus $6.837bn, a 60.4% margin.
Q3'26 reported GAAP EPS $0.35 vs GS est $0.43 and consensus $0.16. Reported free cash flow was -$9.805bn vs GS est -$2.929bn and consensus -$11.627bn.
Q1'27 revenue guidance from management is $33-37bn, well ahead of GS and Street estimates. Q4'26 capex guidance of $35-40bn is above GS and Street estimates.
GS estimates (not reported): Q4'26 revenue $23.97bn, GAAP EBIT $4.71bn, GAAP EPS $0.44. FY26E revenue $51.06bn, EPS $0.50. FY27E revenue $192.49bn, EPS $5.52. FY28E revenue $303.12bn, EPS $7.97.
risk_factors: Governance: majority voting power and execution risk concentrated in the Founder & CEO.
Related-party transactions with entities tied to the Founder & CEO, including co-development of Terafab and Macrohard with Tesla and asset purchases of Tesla products.
High capital intensity and cash burn requiring sizable future fund raises, assumed primarily through debt, plus potential equity dilution from stock grants and equity raises.
Space: competition from other launch companies, higher internal allocation of launches, reliance on government contracts, FAA and other regulatory approvals, and fixed-price contract profitability.

Connectivity: competition, reliance on Starship reusability and rapid launch cadence, scaling enterprise and government contracts, third-party partners for distribution and spectrum, and satellite licensing delays.

SI: orbital datacenter compute is unproven, competition from other frontier AI models, scaling consumer AI revenue (X advertising and X/Grok subscriptions), reliance on Starship launch capacity, and supply chain dependence on third-party chips such as NVDA GPUs.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 breaks out GS estimates of SI Solutions & Infrastructure revenue into hosting (IaaS) deals and other revenue, with YE nameplate compute rising from 1,700MW in 3Q26 to 2,720MW in 4Q26E and 10,025MW in 4Q27E. GS notes many figures, including revenue per MW and implied MWs leased per deal, are its own estimates and not confirmed by the company.
vol_and_positioning: Lock-up expirations are flagged as a source of stock flow and trading dynamics that will influence performance in coming quarters.
Shares trade about 25% below the peak post-IPO close. 3m absolute performance is +23.3% and +19.0% relative to the S&P 500. 3m ADTV is $13.5bn.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand for compute outstrips supply, new compute pays back in under 1 year (possibly about 6 months in 2027), and Q1'27 revenue guidance of $33-37bn is well above Street, supporting the Buy and $245 target.
tension_points.bear_case: Q4'26 capex of $35-40bn and elevated capital intensity through 2027 imply future capital raises that GS expects to act as an overhang until funding visibility improves. GS FY27E free cash flow is -$172.0bn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Failure to scale compute to the guided 2.5-3GW by YE26, or Starship not proving out full reusability and rapid launch cadence.
